transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-08-17
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Javier (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (Orionix - Head of ML), Priya Rao (Orionix Eng Manager), Samir Desai (Orionix Infra), Hana Ito (Orionix NLP Lead)

Summary: Quick discovery call to map Orionix's internationalization needs, context window targets (32k vs 64k), tool-calling (shipment tracking / TMS API), and deployment constraints (data residency, VPC/KMS). Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Action items and follow-ups agreed.

Topics: model selection (open models), context length and KV cache behavior, multilingual performance (EN/JA/ES/AR), tool-calling reliability and fallbacks, security/compliance (SOC2, KMS), demo/bench next steps.

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick intros? we'll go 1-2 minutes each.
[00:12] Alex Chen: Hi I'm Alex, head of ML at Orionix, we run routing optimization and customer-facing chat for logistics across APAC/EMEA. We're exploring LLMs for multimodal customer support and async doc summarization.
[00:24] Priya: Priya here, engineering manager, owning product integration. Main concern is latency and cost across regions.
[00:31] Samir: Samir, infra, looking at networking/KMS and compliance.
[00:36] Hana: Hana, lead NLP, focusing on model quality in Japanese and Arabic, and tool-calling reliability.
[00:43] Maya: Great. Quick context from our side - Liam and Javier are SEs who will run through model tradeoffs and ops. We're primarily looking at whether Redwood Hosted will suffice or if Dedicated/Private makes sense.
[00:56] Liam: Hi all. A few warmup q's - what's your peak qps for chat and what are p95 latency goals?
[01:05] Priya: For chat, interactive UI: peak is about 90 req/s during EU/JP peaks, p95 target is ~200-250ms for short prompts, but for long context summarization we can accept higher on async flows. Cost target is important, want to keep per-req infra low.
[01:22] Alex: Also we need to keep conversation history up to 32k tokens today but pilot teams want to test 64k for contract/manifest summarization.
[01:32] Hana: For Japanese and Arabic we see present hallucination issues with some open models; tone and politeness in JA is important.
[01:41] Javier: Helpful. When you say 64k, is that the working set or full KV cache? do you need full attention over 64k or prefix caching is fine?
[01:50] Hana: For manifests we need extraction across long doc, so full attention for certain ops - prefer single-shot summary.
[01:59] Liam: Ok. High-level model options we typically evaluate: Llama2-13B / 70B variants (open weights), Mistral-7B and variants, Mixtral / Mistral-instructs, and some emergent community 8-bit quantized mixes. Redwood has verified perf profiles for these. For 64k we look at models with efficient attention or windowing and KV cache strategies.
[02:21] Alex: Any models you see perform better on non-English? We care about JA/AR and some Spanish.
[02:28] Javier: Mistral variants tend to be strong on European languages; Japanese sometimes needs fine-tuning or LoRA on tokenization differences. For Arabic we often see narrow-domain drop unless you have pretraining/exposure. We recommend evals with your real datasets.
[02:43] Priya: On the deployment side, what's the Hosted vs Dedicated break point? When do you recommend moving to Dedicated?
[02:50] Liam: If you need predictable latency under sustained 80-100 qps and want isolation/compliance, Dedicated makes sense. Hosted is fastest to go-live and lower ops lift but you trade off some isolation and reserved throughput. Private (VPC/on-prem) is for strict data residency and KMS control.
[03:07] Samir: For Private, can we bring our own KMS HSM and still use Redwood control plane?
[03:13] Maya: Yes, Private offers customer-managed KMS/HSM and a private control plane option. We can show network diagram.
[03:19] Hana: On tool-calling, reliability is crucial. We call shipping API endpoints (tracking, TMS updates). If LLM makes a bad API call, we need deterministic retries and blocking safeguards. How does Redwood handle function-calling and fallbacks?
[03:33] Liam: We support structured function/tool calling with schema enforcement and also offer runtime-level policies: automatic verification hooks, and for Dedicated/Private you get tracing hooks and retry policies. For Hosted we provide recommended safe defaults plus ability to inspect call logs.
[03:46] Alex: What about throughput for streaming responses while also doing function calls? We might stream partial summaries while tool-calling in parallel.
[03:54] Javier: There's an architectural pattern we usually recommend: separate streams for UI tokens and tool outputs, use async tool execution with callback to the user. We'll show an example flow in the deep-dive.
[04:07] Priya: Cost question - rough delta between Hosted per-token and Dedicated reserved?
[04:13] Maya: Hosted is usage-based; Dedicated has an upfront reserved capacity. For sustained high qps Dedicated generally lowers per-token unit cost maybe 30-50% depending on model and quantization. We'll send a comparative spreadsheet.
[04:26] Hana: On quantization - some models degrade on JA/AR when aggressively quantized. Any guidance?
[04:33] Liam: Yes, 4-bit quant helps cost but we often recommend mixed precision/quantization profiles per model. Redwood Optimize suggests per-workload quant profiles and flags quality regressions. We'll run a small test on your JA/AR dataset.
[04:45] Alex: Security checklist - we need SOC2, SSO with SAML, RBAC, audit logs with token-level trace. Do you provide encrypted logs?
[04:53] Maya: We have SOC2, SAML/SSO, RBAC, and audit logs. For Private you can configure encrypted audit retention in your KMS. We'll attach our compliance pack.
[05:04] Samir: Latency: you mentioned <250ms; our EU customers are sensitive. What's your p95 for Mistral-7B vs Llama2-13B on say A10G equiv?
[05:13] Liam: Roughly, Mistral-7B quantized can hit ~80-120ms p95 for short prompts on A10G-like hardware. Llama2-13B is a bit heavier: ~140-220ms depending on quant and sequence length. We'll provide your exact perf curves with our recommended quant kernels.
[05:28] Hana: For 64k tests, how do you instrument KV cache warmups?
[05:33] Javier: We measure cold start vs warmed KV cache. For long-document single-shot, warm cache doesn't help much because full attention is required; but for interactive chat with growing context, KV cache and prefix caching reduces token regen. We'll show our instrumentation dashboards in the deep-dive.
[05:49] Alex: Competitor question - some of our procurement folks asked about OpenAI function calling reliability. Why pick Redwood?
[05:56] Maya: Two reasons: 1) unified runtime across Hosted/Dedicated/Private so you can start Hosted then move to Private without rewriting integrations; 2) cost/perf controls and observability geared for ops teams (per-token cost breakdown, rollouts, automated fallbacks). We also support customer-provided models in Private.
[06:14] Priya: Major blockers for us: 1) SOC2 + data residency for EU/JP, 2) predictable latency at scale, 3) multilingual QA. If Redwood can show examples addressing each, procurement is comfortable.
[06:27] Maya: Totally. Action plan: we'll send the perf + cost spreadsheet, SOC2 docs, and propose a Dedicated trial. Also schedule the 64k/kv deep-dive next week.
[06:37] Hana: Also send a small prompt set template for JA/AR so we can run quick evals.
[06:42] Liam: We'll include a starter harness and suggested prompt files.
[06:45] Maya: Anything else from Orionix?
[06:48] Alex: No, that's it. Thanks everyone.
[06:51] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up with materials.

End of transcript.
